item.title: Unvirtual Reality: Re: Unvirtual Reality
item.content:encoded:
Alright, I have given it a lot of thought and I came with these two solutions to give it more flavour and character:

1 - Adding a countdown:
While the SCP loads it could show a progress bar and have under it some strange text like "Blurring Reality Lines", "Mitigating Time-Stream Discontinuities", "Atomizing Atomic Particles", "Calibrating Dr. Bright" and one of the messages could be "Calculating next auto-simulacra event: X days."

The foundation would discover that "Calculating next auto-simulacra event" refers to the days remaining until they become a new "simulation" and end suffering a SCP breach and one of their personnel becomes controlled by an exterior force.

The only way of stopping this would be using the SCP itself, as with each simulation that they do the "Calculating next auto-simulacra event" value randomly changes.

This would force the Foundation of the baseline reality to continuously use the SCP, forcing its staff to put their alternate versions in danger. The simulations could also generate stress, nightmares and sentiment of regret in the people that play them, specially if their alternate selves died during the simulation and if they know that it isn't a simulation, but real. Amnesics are recommenced after someone uses the SCP.

2 - Adding a trap:
The SCP article could have a collapsible with a name like "Explanation and inner workings of SCP-XXXX's phenomena" and when opened it would reveal that there is no explanation nor understanding of how the SCP works, but that the mere act of opening the collapsible has informed several MTF groups of your location and that you have ousted yourself as a spy from a parallel universe, and that as long as the breach lasts you will be tortured for information.

item.title: Wrong Place Wrong Time: Re: Wrong Place Wrong Time
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the feedback. I don't want to sound argumentative, but I would ike to address your points just to see if I'm on the right track to fix it or let it go.

Okay, it's been a while since I used a forum and don't know how to hide text, if any admins want to condense the following, go ahead and please tell me how.

-Actually, a third option for how he got it, Church of Maxwell does a charity fundraiser. Prosthetics are expensive, especially magical ones, and when a regular guy can't afford it, some people help him, but what price does that help come at?
-Maybe I leave out Twisted Pines, I felt I had to because of how SCP-2806 fits in, but really I just want this to fit in the Resurrection Canon, but I'm kind of getting ahead of myself either way, so maybe I should cut that from this draft.
-as far as the Lawgiver being an insurance policy, it's not that the character is not trustworthy, but I think it's a bit farfetched to assume that the Foundation knows they can trust him, so they partner him up just in case and over time he proves himself while also earning the loyalty of his partner. Remember, this is an ordinary civilian who just suddenly shows up with an anomaly and the Foundation is on the edge on whether to keep him or cut him, he doesn't just get his free pass all at once.
-Olympia and Black Queen, I apologize for name dropping them, I believe I will cut their names from the pitch. I actually did think out very important and relevant purposes for both of them,but since they are so big meeting someone so small, they will be introduced in subtle ways using aliases, and I kind of ruined it, but I wanted to make sure it was okay to use them at all. Olympia is not actually the original Olympia, but one of the copies that was customized for a specific purpose so while she is ridiculously perfect for that job, she is surprisingly average at everything else, so her role is to be reliably secure for one aspect of the story while still not being too overpowered and an instant answer to everything else. I like the idea behind her, but I need to use her carefully or she can go off the rails fast. She actually won't be using the name Olympia to differentiate from the original she was cloned from and won't even be fully identified until a later story, so while I know who she is, I'm going to cut the name because it's just clutter. And Black Queen is just going to make an exposition cameo which I hope will be a seed for something exciting down the road, but for now due to her nature she won't even use any name at all. The way she fits in is that she sees my character as potentially useful in her plans but needs to test him to see if he will do what she wants so she sets events in motion, but is disappointed in the results and abandons him, but not before making a huge difference. I suppose I could just use a completely different character, but I actually have an idea for something bigger later, but the question is, will we ever get to that point in the story that I need to go there now?
-Skywalker Protocol is actually my biggest obstacle. I read it as "here's all the cybernetics you could want, and the one hitch that prevents you from going Mary Sue" so the challenge is that in this interview he says enough to get the Foundation's attention and he gets spared. Admittedly, trying to explain this exception may be impressive if I can pull it off but also the biggest reason I should probably scrap this entirely if I can't pull that off. And again, perhaps I jumped the gun by mentioning Alpha-9. He won't actually be joining right away. This tale just focuses on the interview introducing the characters and leaving their fates vague, and assuming it goes well I follow it up with the next part where a security breach prevents him from going through Skywalker Protocol. Then there's a series of events in which he goes from being one of the breaches to help recontain the other SCPs, mostly because he's terrified and just does whatever he can to survive. After a series of tales resiolving the many plot threads that develop, he finally gets the offer, take the easy way out and forget this ever happened, or join Alpha-9 and he gets to keep the arm in exchange for continuing to help the Foundation.

item.title: Knock Box (Seeking Greenlighting): Re: Knock Box (Seeking Greenlighting)
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there XR Titan. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So I’m mainly confused: what do a black box, pulling items out of it Doraemon-style, video games and a heart attack have to do in common? The concept sounds like a mish-mash of different ideas in order for you to make it sound as cool as possible. When looked at as a whole, however, do you not see how the concept doesn’t have a central theme, message or even effect?

Ideally, you would want to choose one or two main anomalous effects and stick with them, explain them and derive a story from them. If opening a black box causes a heart attack, for example, cool. Why? What causes this upon opening it? Could it be related to what the user finds or sees on the inside? Likewise, if the opening a black box gives you items, cool. What kind of items? Are they related to the user’s childhood memories, e.g.? You see where I’m going with this? Any effect you introduce to the concept should be thematically linked in some way.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll try my best to reply again. All the best!

item.title: SCP Idea in need of GREENLIGHT: Re: SCP Idea in need of GREENLIGHT
item.content:encoded:
Atention grabber is what brings attention to your article, usually the main aspect of it and what makes it unique, or connections to other SCPs, folklore or mythology, connections to real life people and events. In other words, the things that might catch the reader's attention. In your case it could be the connection to the mystery of the Bermuda Triangle.

On a side note, you have a very basic and bare idea. It would be good to flesh out this concept, specifically the part of the narrative. The story you want to tell is more important than just describing the creature. Hope you find a way to get this idea out there!

item.title: Abandoned idea: move along lol: Re: A Very Sadistic Cap [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Sand

So the SCP got bored with what it was doing, so it starts a secret magic cult where abuse and torture is a way of life. The cult gives the SCP a more appropriate form than a hat. The cult starts to grow, and the SCP decided to want to create a dystopian world where people are tortured and sacrificed for its own entertainment (too edgy?) An MTF unit has been ordered to find the cult, stop its growth, and neutralize the SCP before that ever happens.

So basically, there's gonna be some explorations logs of what the MTF finds along the way. While they're trying to locate where the cult is, The cult gets stronger and stronger, so MTF has to hurry before the SCP causes major havoc around the world.

This still doesn't really show much on how and why the skip is like this, the narrative seems more focused on showing it being evil and dangerous (which on its own isn't interesting or inherently engaging), rather than expanding on the questions the concept raised and building up to the payoff over the course of the narrative. Along with this, the proposed narrative doesn't give any context as to how the Foundation found out about the cult, or why they decided that they had to kill it, considering they are against killing anomalies if they can avoid it.

+ show block
– hide block

I thought of another story where the SCP actually achieved world domination, and the whole story is gonna revolve around a man that writes in his journal and describes how life was affected after the SCP took over the world. He and the group of strangers that he's stuck with lives in an abandoned bomb shelter to hide from the wraith of the SCP. He and one of the members of the group volunteer to go outside into the apocalyptic environment to scavenge basic necessities to survive, but they get into trouble along the way.

For the most part, this has the same issues as the first proposed narrative. With the addition of the Foundation being out of the picture, considering this would be written from their perspective, it's odd that they're not mentioned at all.- I have trouble believing they would have been wiped out by this, considering they have dealt with end of world scenarios before.

Journal entry narratives can work very well, however they need to be unique in their own way, they need to have something that will make them stand out. Currently this doesn't really show anything inherently new or interesting, which makes it feel a bit un-engaging. Along with this, the narrative shows little to nothing on the skip itself, there's no real context or information to be learnt from this. How would the draft look if there was little to nothing on the skip itself?

Overall, the both proposed narratives don't seem to focus on the skip or the Foundations quarrels with it much, as they seem more focused on depicting blood and gore, with no context behind it. Which (to me) comes off as a bit edgy, and a quick way to keep audience attention, by raising the stakes and/or making the skip more dangerous.

Cheers,

RED

item.title: Anomalous-D: Anomalous-D
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch

Anomalous-D (AD) is an extradimensional parasite which feeds on the pain, fear, grief or rage of other sentient entities. It became entangled with our reality and assumed human form eventually finding its way into a Foundation D Class assignment after being captured and convicted of a string of sadistic crimes against animals and people. Its position as a D Class brings it into frequent close proximity of various other anomalies. Anomalous D devises novel ways provoke or torture these anomalies undetected so that it can feed off their pain and rage.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:

  • Containment procedure
  • Description of Entity
  • Description of how the creature came to be in containment / details of anomalous nature
  • Addenda:
    • Incident report: Containment breach first drawing scrutiny of AD
    • Memo: List of incident reports possibly involving AD
    • Interview: Log of the interview which reveals AD’s status as anomalous.
    • Interview: Log of feeding procedure
    • Memo: Detailing the variability of AD’s appearance
    • Memo: Possible reclassification as Keter / Thaumiel

Hook / Attention Grabber:

Following a major incident, the Foundation has confined it but is not sure that it is completely contained. Still, the possibility that this new anomaly may be used to injure or possibly destroy other anomalies is cannot be ignored.

Additional Notes:

Anomalous D typically resides between dimensions and might encounter various manifestations of other trans-dimensional creatures on its travels. It would not normally be able to feed on these entities as they would either be too powerful or impossible to hold on to. But in this reality it has found itself – quite accidentally – in a situation where the SCP foundation has trapped them and rendered them unable to defend themselves. Its motivation is to feed on their stress while not getting snared itself.

I expect that I’ll need lots of discussion and refinement to get this where I want it to be. This would be my first SCP contribution and I’m not an experienced writer. Additionally, most of what interests me in this concept are its possibilities for world-building and future story-telling. It will be challenging to bring this to life in a way that hooks the reader while also pointing to the other possibilities.

item.title: Negative-Safe Entity: Re: Negative-Safe Entity
item.content:encoded: I have to say, I’m a big fan of creative containment, so you've already got me there. I have three main notes for this concept. First, I think you should be more specific as to what the properties of this anomaly are. Do they manifest cells around them and the resources go missing or do they steal the resources and actively build the cells? This isn’t that big of a deal, I just think it should be clear. Second, I would call this Thaumiel instead of Safe. After all the Foundation’s using it to build cells for other SCPs. The third is more of a recommendation for writing. I wouldn’t recommend making this too long of an article. You’re mentioning interviews and tying this into other SCPs and that’s all fine, I just want to make sure you aren’t going to be running on one idea the whole time. Because I like this concept and I think it’d make for an interesting article, but there isn’t much to say about it from what I’m seeing so make sure not to repeat yourself.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight - Self-Casting Spell: Seeking Greenlight - Self-Casting Spell
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A thaumaturgical sentient life-form, living deep in syberia, their culture with strong Polish influences left by Sybiraks. (Sybiraks were the Polish people resettled to Syberia.) It explores both the effects of Polish diaspora and the foundation containing a society.

Central Narrative: It starts off with the special containment procedures (the fenced off part of syberia), then there is a description (about how their bodies are made of what is basically sigils, about how they exchange spells that modify them as plasmids). Then it describes their culture, and the addeneum, where it is described how the sybiraks discover them and describe them, and offer them vodka and rabbit's blood, and how their societies get together, learning from each other and “forming a symbiosis”. It ends with the Incident, when they almost had a civil war.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The concept, I think. Also the ala genetics that arise inside them, and the weird stuff that arises cause of sentient beings being able to trade plasmids.

Additional Notes: Catholic sentient spells, which form tribes. An idea so weird, that it can work. Also their tribe is divided into three groups:
The Ultracatholics, lead by a Fanatical Pariah Priest, who want to make the other groups just as catholic.
The Tolerant, lead by the youngest of the elders, who want to cooperate with The Foundation, and to learn more of the outside world
The Traditionalists, lead by their shaman, who want to be freed and allowed to go back to the old Yakut ways.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror: Re: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror
item.content:encoded:
Hi! Thanks for getting back to me.

I think I overused the word “exact” in my description here, it should say “similar.” The events are not exactly the same, and it leaves room for a couple of interpretations of what the anomaly actually IS. The second foundation is introduced early on, what I’m going for is for the reader to debate with themselves throughout the article or at the end with whether the PCS Foundation is anomalous, if they’re non-anomalous and have been abusing anomalies to avoid detection, or if NONE of it is anomalous. The SCP Foundation themselves will be having this debate alongside the reader, the addendum will be riddled with Staff Surveys (that the reader can also take) to attempt to get a general consensus on what they believe the PCS foundation to be/be doing so that they can work with certainties, and at the end, our three theories will be proposed in three separate theory documents.
